title: Immutable release selectors and runtime resolution matrix
creator: Maya Chen
description: Define unambiguous semantics for model version selectors accepted by the Redwood API/SDK and the runtime resolver. Covers pin-by-tag (including wildcard/tag namespaces), semver ranges, and immutable commit/hash pins. Specifies precedence rules, runtime fallback behavior, effects on performance-profile binding, and compatibility guarantees across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments.
acceptance_criteria: API accepts and validates three selector families: tag (e.g., 'stable', 'release/2025-02'), semver (e.g., '^1.2.0', '>=2.0.0 <3.0.0'), and commit hash (full or short sha).
Resolver precedence is documented and deterministic: exact hash > exact semver version > semver range > exact tag > tag-wildcard > latest-compatible fallback.
Wildcard tag semantics defined (single '*' wildcard allowed in right-most component of tag namespace) and examples provided.

Performance profile publishing is tied to the resolved immutable model ref (full commit hash). Profiles referenced in user configs must be rewritten by system to point to resolved hash to avoid silent drift.

Runtime implements resolution matrix that guarantees identical behavior in Hosted, Dedicated, and Private (VPC) modes given same selector and model catalog snapshot. Any divergence must be surfaced as a resolved_ref mismatch event.
SDKs surface a clear ModelResolution object with: requested_selector, resolved_ref (immutable hash), resolved_semver, applied_profile_id, and resolution_path (list of steps as strings).
Automated unit and integration tests cover selector parsing, precedence edge-cases, cross-region resolution, and performance-profile binding.
technical_notes: We will treat commit-hash pins as canonical immutable refs. Any selector that resolves to a different commit over time is considered a different resolved_ref.

Semver resolution is performed against the model registry index at the time of request. For Dedicated/Private deployments with periodic sync, we record the registry snapshot id used for resolution in the SDK response.
Tag namespace: '<channel>/<name>' where channel is optional. Wildcard syntax allowed for the right-most component only, e.g., 'experimental/*' matches 'experimental/xla-2025-01' but not 'exp/*/foo'.
Precedence rationale: favor immutability (hash) and exactness (exact semver) to minimize unexpected behavior for production traffic. Tags are convenience aliases and therefore lower precedence.

When a selector cannot be resolved in the local catalog, runtime will attempt fallback candidates according to precedence rules. Fallbacks must be opt-in per-route (route config flag 'allow_runtime_fallback=true').

Publishing performance profiles: when a model is onboarded or profiled, the system will create a binding of profile -> resolved_ref. If a user pins by tag/semver, we will translate the bound profile to the resolved_ref at deploy time to ensure stability.
rollout_plan: Draft API changes behind feature flag 'pinning-v2'. Release cadence: internal SDKs preview -> GA API change. Step 1: catalog + registry snapshot id included in /models and /resolve endpoints. Step 2: SDKs return ModelResolution object. Step 3: enforce profile->resolved_ref rewrite in Console and Deploy flows.
testing_plan: Unit tests for selector parser covering malformed selectors, semver edge-cases, and wildcard tag grammar.
Integration test: Hosted vs Dedicated resolution parity using same snapshot id; assert identical resolved_ref and applied_profile_id.
Chaos test: simulate registry sync lag for Dedicated and ensure resolved_ref mismatch event generated and surfacing to Console.
E2E: customer route pinning by '^2.1.0' should continue to serve identical binary artifacts after model catalog updates when resolved_ref is pinned in rollout config.
updates: 2025-02-03 - Ticket created by Maya Chen. Initial proposal drafted; goal to eliminate silent profile drift and clarify wildcard tag semantics.
2025-02-06 - Engineering sync: agreed to three selector families (tag, semver, hash). Lars to draft resolver precedence matrix and SDK surface shape.

2025-02-10 - Prototype resolver implemented in catalog service. Early finding: semver ranges against prerelease labels require canonicalization. Decided to normalize prerelease tokens per semver spec, with explicit mapping in registry metadata.
2025-02-14 - Discussed Dedicated/Private snapshot model with Infra. Plan: include 'registry_snapshot_id' in resolution responses for non-hosted deployments to allow deterministic replay.

2025-02-18 - Security review kickoff. Pinning affects data residency and reproducibility; security requested audit events on all resolved_ref changes for enterprise customers. Assigned ENG-31418 to add audit log events.
2025-02-20 - Updated acceptance criteria to require SDK ModelResolution.resolution_path (list of steps). Began writing integration tests.
